facts.text: Talus beside the glacier remnants is very loose in September; a block slid onto one climber's leg
The ridge rock is rotten and sheds blocks easily, so wear a helmet and keep clear of anyone below
The true summit pinnacle lies well along the ridge from where you first gain it; allow extra time for that traverse
By late September, crossing the low-angle ice patch on foot was easier than the choss beside it
Microspikes or crampons and an axe for the remaining ice (September)

notes: West Ridge, West Route, Southeast Route (and probably East Route) all start from La Bohn Gap via Necklace Valley and may be one line filed several times; track given only to West Ridge, whose name matches the logged route exactly. None of the five routes has a Summit pin, and none of the packet routes has a Trailhead pin other than a text name. Web sources say the Hinman Glacier is now mostly a snowfield/ice patch.
